LOL
EL-oh-EL (also LAWL)
interjection (Millennial slang)
Acronym for laughing out loud (early on also lots of love, a sense that caused famous parental misunderstandings). Wayne Pearson has claimed coining it on the Viewline bulletin board in Calgary in the 1980s, and it circulated on Usenet by 1989. AOL chat rooms and AOL Instant Messenger (1997) made it universal; texting in the 2000s softened it from real laughter into a tone marker that means "I am being friendly" ("lol ok," "sorry lol"). The Oxford English Dictionary admitted it in 2011. Gen Z largely retired it for skull emojis and keyboard-smash.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

LOL began as "laughing out loud" and became the Millennial generation’s punctuation: a lowercase lol at the end of a sentence now rarely means anyone laughed. It softens a request, cushions criticism, or covers embarrassment. The Christian observation: laughter itself is a gift of God, and the Bible is not embarrassed by it. There is "A time to weep, and a time to laugh" (Ecc 3:4); when the Lord turned again the captivity of Zion, "Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing" (Psa 126:2); "A merry heart doeth good like a medicine" (Pro 17:22). A Christian home should ring with real laughter. But the reflexive lol is mostly not laughter; it is a mask. Scripture knew the mask too: "Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth is heaviness" (Pro 14:13). The habit can blunt honesty ("just kidding lol"), take the edge off a cruelty, or hide real pain behind three letters. A father reads his teenager’s texts not for the jokes but for the lol at the end of something sad, and asks about it. He teaches his children to laugh with their whole hearts at what is truly funny, and to say plainly what they mean when it is not.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial acronym (1980s BBS / Usenet; AIM and texting 2000s) for laughing out loud, worn down into a tone-softener; laughter is a gift (Ecc 3:4), but the reflexive lol can mask sorrow or cruelty (Pro 14:13).

LOL, interj. (Millennial chat and text slang, 1980s–2010s; acronym of laughing out loud) Expressing amusement; by the 2000s chiefly a softener or tone marker. "lol ok." Variants: lolz, lulz (mischievous amusement), LOLing.

Admitted to the Oxford English Dictionary 2011; spoken aloud as "lawl."

Webster (1828), root laugh: LAUGH, verb intransitive l’aff. [Heb.] 1. To make the noise and exhibit the features which are characteristic of mirth in the human species. Violent laughter is accompanied with a shaking of the sides, and all laughter expels breath from the lungs. 2. In poetry, to be gay; to appear gay, cheerful, pleasant, lively or brilliant. Then laughs the childish year with flow’rets crown’d. And o’er the foaming bowl, the laughing wine. To laugh at, to ridicule; to treat with some degree of contempt. […]

Decode for parents: look for the lol after something sad; it is often a hand raised for help.

Key Scripture

Ecc 3:4 — "A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;"

Psa 126:2 — "Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing: then said they among the heathen, The LORD hath done great things for them."

Pro 17:22 — "A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones."

Pro 14:13 — "Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth is heaviness."

Eph 5:4 — "Neither filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting, which are not convenient: but rather giving of thanks."

Modern Corruption

LOL wore laughter down into a mask that softens, hides, and excuses; Scripture blesses real laughter and sees the sorrowful heart beneath false mirth.

expand to see more

The quiet corruption of lol is dishonesty by habit. It lets a hard word be said and disowned in the same breath, lets cruelty pass as banter, and lets a hurting child report something serious in a tone that asks no one to take it seriously. Paul names the vice of speech that is witty without being wholesome: "filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting, which are not convenient: but rather giving of thanks" (Eph 5:4). Not all jesting is condemned there, but the jest that dodges truth and responsibility is.

The recovery is to restore laughter to its place and to recover plain speech. Real laughter, at a good story, at the baby’s first word, at our own folly, is a foretaste of the joy of the redeemed. The fake laughter of the reflexive acronym is a small lie told a thousand times a week. Teach the young to laugh out loud when something is funny, and to say "I’m hurting," "I’m sorry," or "I disagree" without three letters to hide behind.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English hlihhan (laugh) → 1980s BBS / Usenet acronym LOL → 1997 AIM → 2000s texting tone-marker → 2011 OED.

Old English hlihhan — to laugh

1980s: LOL on bulletin boards; 1989 on Usenet

1997–2000s: AIM, chat rooms, texting; meaning softens to a tone marker
